name: main
prose: Precondition: the program runs on a Linux system with hugetlb support; argv[0] is used as the memfd_create name. Postcondition (main, hugetlb-madvise.c:60-367; slice cut the head): it reads the default huge page size and calls exit(1) with a message if it is 0 (the following 'base page size' check repeats the test of huge_page_size, so a zero base page size is not detected); it reads the number of free huge pages and calls exit(KSFT_SKIP) if fewer than MIN_FREE_PAGES (20) are free; it creates a hugetlb memfd (exit(1) on failure). It then runs a sequence of tests of MADV_DONTNEED, MADV_REMOVE, fallocate and fallocate(PUNCH_HOLE) on anonymous and memfd hugetlb mappings (NR_HUGE_PAGES = 10 pages each), after each step comparing the free huge page count with the expected value through validate_free_pages, which prints a message and calls exit(1) on a mismatch. Each mmap, the paired munmap calls at the beginning, each madvise and fallocate call whose success or failure is being tested prints a message and calls exit(1) when the result is not the expected one. The intermediate cleanups and the final two munmap calls are written '(void)munmap(...)' and close(fd) is called without checking, so a failure of those calls does not change the outcome. If every check passes it returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the (void)munmap calls (hugetlb-madvise.c:133, 170, 195, 254, 294, 362-363) and the final close(fd) (365) are not checked, so main can return 0 even if they fail; the old prose said it returns 0 only if every syscall succeeded. Slice cut the head; real function main.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: main never returns to its caller; it sets a 9-test plan, obtains a free base address via find_base_addr (whose mmap or munmap failure exits with a failure message without dumping maps), then runs eight MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE mmap checks that require success for the 5-page mapping at base, the 3-page mapping at base+page_size, and the 1-page mappings at base and base+4*page_size, and require MAP_FAILED (without checking errno) for the 5-page mapping at base, the 1-page mapping at base+2*page_size, the 2-page mapping at base+3*page_size, and the 2-page mapping at base, dumping the process maps and exiting with failure on any unexpected mmap result or on any munmap failure in main, then performs the ninth check by munmapping the 5-page base range (dumping maps and exiting with failure if that munmap fails), and finally calls ksft_finished, which exits the process with overall success if all checks passed.
note: prose re-checked against map_fixed_noreplace.c:41-201 (8 mmap calls, 2 of main's own munmap calls, find_base_addr failure paths, ksft_finished exit) and kept; reviewer points from rounds 0/2 (errno not checked; 9th check is munmap; find_base_addr exits without dump_maps) are already in the prose. Contract dropped: main exits through ksft_finished and touches the process address space, outside method rule 4.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, mprotect_WRITE_EXEC)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, mprotect_WRITE_EXEC) (mdwe_test.c:259-272); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags and, for enabled variants, the memory-deny-write-execute prctl state (executable_map_should_fail(variant) is variant->enabled && (!variant->forked || variant->inherit)). Postcondition: it maps self->size bytes of PROT_WRITE memory into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED, which stops the test on failure), then calls mprotect(self->p, self->size, PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC) and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_LT or EXPECT_EQ) unless the result is negative when executable_map_should_fail(variant) is true, or 0 when it is false. The mapping stays in self->p and is unmapped by the fixture teardown.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against mdwe_test.c:168-171 and 259-272; the prose is kept in substance, with the gtest-style 'TestBody' wording replaced by the real TEST_F-generated function. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, mmap_FIXED)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, mmap_FIXED) (mdwe_test.c:274-285); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags. Postcondition: it maps self->size bytes of PROT_READ memory into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), then maps self->size bytes at the same address with PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC and flags | MAP_FIXED, replacing the existing mapping, and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_EQ) unless the returned address equals self->p. self->p is unchanged and the mapping is unmapped by the fixture teardown.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against mdwe_test.c:274-285; kept in substance. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, arm64_BTI)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, arm64_BTI) (mdwe_test.c:287-301); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags. Postcondition: on a build for aarch64 it skips the test and returns if getauxval(AT_HWCAP2) does not report HWCAP2_BTI; on any other architecture the HWCAP test is compiled out and the SKIP statement (SKIP(return, "HWCAP2_BTI not supported")) then executes unconditionally, so the test always skips and returns before doing anything. When it does not skip it maps self->size bytes with PROT_EXEC into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), calls mprotect(self->p, self->size, PROT_EXEC | PROT_BTI) and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_EQ) unless it returns 0.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: outside __aarch64__ the SKIP is unconditional (mdwe_test.c:291-294), so the old precondition (which required HWCAP2_BTI only for aarch64 builds and implied a run elsewhere) was incomplete. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mprotect_faulted_left_unfaulted_right)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mprotect_faulted_left_unfaulted_right) (merge.c:266-323); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range of at least 11 pages and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps 9 anonymous private pages (PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_FIXED) at carveout + 2 * page_size (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), makes the last 3 pages read-only (splitting the VMA), faults in only the first page by writing ptr[0] = 'x' (which gives the left VMA an anon_vma), makes the first 3 pages read-only, then makes the middle 3 pages read-only too (each mprotect asserted to return 0), so that the three VMAs should merge. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that a VMA containing ptr exists and that it spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 9 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: only the first page (ptr[0]) is written, not the first six pages (merge.c:299); the other pages stay unfaulted. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mprotect_unfaulted_left_faulted_right)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mprotect_unfaulted_left_faulted_right) (merge.c:325-382); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range of at least 11 pages and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps 9 anonymous private pages (PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_FIXED) at carveout + 2 * page_size (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), makes the first 3 pages read-only (splitting the VMA), faults in only page 3 by writing ptr[3 * page_size] = 'x' (which gives the right VMA an anon_vma), makes the last 3 pages read-only, then makes the middle 3 pages read-only (each mprotect asserted to return 0), so that the three VMAs should merge. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that a VMA containing ptr exists and spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 9 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: only ptr[3 * page_size] is written, not the last six pages (merge.c:358). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted) (merge.c:748-831; the packet name mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted_faulted does not exist and the slice starts mid-test); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps three 5-page anonymous private read/write areas ptr, ptr2 and ptr3 with MAP_FIXED at carveout offsets 1, 7 and 14 pages, moves ptr3 2000 pages further away and ptr2 1000 pages further away with mremap(MREMAP_MAYMOVE | MREMAP_FIXED), faults in ptr and ptr3 by writing their first byte (ptr2 stays unfaulted), moves ptr3 back to &ptr[10 * page_size] and moves ptr2 to &ptr[5 * page_size] (each mremap asserted not to fail), so that ptr and ptr2 should merge but ptr3 should stay separate. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that the VMA containing ptr spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 10 * page_size) and that the VMA containing ptr3 spans exactly [ptr3, ptr3 + 5 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: slice cut the head; named by the real test TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted). The old prose (a 'still-rejected' item) described this test but called its mappings preconditions of the caller; the whole setup is in the test itself (merge.c:763-822).

name: get_sqrt
prose: Precondition: val is an unsigned long less than 1099511627776 (1TB), so that mid*mid (mid <= 2^19) fits in unsigned long and the initial high bound 2^20 covers the square root of val. Postcondition: because high is decremented unconditionally on every iteration (there is no else branch), the function returns 1 when val is 0; when val equals m*m for some power of two m (1 <= m <= 524288) it returns that m; in every other case it returns m+1, where m is the largest power of two with m*m < val and val < 4*m*m — so the result is generally not the integer square root of val.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= val && val < 1099511627776; ensures (val == 0 ==> result == 1) && (val >= 1 ==> ((result * result == val && (result & (result - 1)) == 0) || (((result - 1) & (result - 2)) == 0 && (result - 1) * (result - 1) < val && val < 4 * (result - 1) * (result - 1)))); */
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: for val = 16 the code returns 4 (mid takes the values 2^19, 2^18, ... so mid = 4 gives temp == 16 and the function returns mid, mremap_test.c:91-92), which satisfies the first disjunct of the contract; I also simulated the loop for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65, 1e9, 2^38, 2^38+1 and 2^40-1 and all results match the prose and the contract. Prose and contract kept.

name: syscall_raw
prose: Precondition: n is a system call number and a1..a6 are its arguments (arguments the call does not use are ignored by the kernel); the file builds only for x86_64, i386 or aarch64 (any other architecture hits an #error). Postcondition (syscall_raw, pkey_sighandler_tests.c:45-78; static inline, always inlined): it issues the system call directly with inline assembly (the 'syscall' instruction on x86_64 with a1..a6 in rdi, rsi, rdx, r10, r8, r9; 'int $0x80' on i386, where a6 is not passed; 'svc #0' on aarch64 with the number in x8) instead of going through glibc's syscall(), so no PLT or library code protected by memory protection key 0 is touched, and returns the raw value left in the return register as a long: a non-negative result, or a negative errno value as set by the kernel (errno itself is not set). The function has no other effects of its own; the effects are those of the system call (for example SYS_exit terminates the calling thread).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:39-78; added the per-architecture argument passing and that errno is not set. Contract left empty (arbitrary system calls).

name: pkey_reg_restrictive_default
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (pkey_reg_restrictive_default, pkey_sighandler_tests.c:103-111; static inline, returns u64): it returns set_pkey_bits(PKEY_REG_ALLOW_NONE, 0, PKEY_DISABLE_ACCESS), i.e. the architecture's 'allow nothing' protection-key register value with the access-disable setting for key 0 applied, which the tests use as their most restrictive register value (the source comment says execution on pkey 0 stays possible so callers need not enable it). It only computes a value, with no side effects.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:99-111. Contract left empty (depends on the macros PKEY_REG_ALLOW_NONE and set_pkey_bits).

name: sigsegv_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGSEGV handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGSEGV, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext. Postcondition: it locks the global mutex, copies *info into the global siginfo, signals the global condition variable, unlocks the mutex, and then issues SYS_exit(0), so the calling thread (SYS_exit ends only the thread) terminates with status 0 and the function does not return; no locks, references or memory remain held.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:113-123 and kept; note SYS_exit ends only the calling thread

name: sigusr1_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGUSR1 handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGUSR1, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext. Postcondition: it locks the global mutex, copies *info into the global siginfo, signals the global condition variable, unlocks the mutex, and returns normally to the interrupted thread, leaving no locks held and no memory allocated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:125-133 and kept

name: sigusr2_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGUSR2 handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGUSR2, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext, with the pkru register at the init_pkru value that enables MPK 0 so library calls work. Postcondition: it prints its invocation message to stdout and returns normally to the interrupted thread, leaving no locks held and no memory allocated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:135-142 and kept

name: raise_sigusr2
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: the function obtains the caller's thread id via SYS_gettid and sends SIGUSR2 to that thread via SYS_tkill; if a SIGUSR2 handler is installed it runs and the signal returns, so this function returns normally to its caller; if no handler is installed the default disposition for SIGUSR2 terminates the process and the function does not return.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:144-156 and kept

name: thread_segv_with_pkey0_disabled
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine whose thread stack is accessible when it begins, and a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it writes the most restrictive pkey register value, disabling access on every protection key including pkey 0, and then dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a SIGSEGV with SEGV_MAPERR at address NULL that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); the function therefore does not return in the tests (its 'return NULL' is only reached if the store does not fault).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:158-166 and kept: the function never returns only when the SIGSEGV handler runs and ends the thread

name: thread_segv_pkuerr_stack
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine whose thread stack is protected by pkey 0, and a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it writes the most restrictive pkey register value, disabling access on every protection key including pkey 0, and then returns NULL; the test expects that returning requires accessing the now-inaccessible stack and so raises a SIGSEGV with SEGV_PKUERR that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); the function therefore does not return in the tests (it is terminated by the handler's SYS_exit).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:168-175 and kept; the SEGV_PKUERR outcome is what the test expects (source comment), not something the C code itself guarantees

name: thread_segv_maperr_ptr
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine and its ptr argument points to a valid, allocated stack_t describing an alternate signal stack that is pkey_mprotect()ed with pkey 0; a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it installs that alternate signal stack via the SYS_sigaltstack syscall, writes a pkey register value that disables every key except pkey 1 (so pkey 0, protecting the thread and signal stacks, is inaccessible), and then dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a SIGSEGV with SEGV_MAPERR at address NULL that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); after the faulting store the source would call SYS_exit(0) and return NULL, but the SIGSEGV handler ends the thread first.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:177-198 and kept; added that the SYS_exit after the faulting store would run only if the fault were not delivered

name: test_sigsegv_handler_with_pkey0_disabled
prose: Precondition: none beyond a working ksft framework. Postcondition: the function installs sigsegv_handler as the SIGSEGV handler with SA_SIGINFO (if sigaction fails it prints an error and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE), so it does not return on that path), clears the global siginfo, creates a detached thread running thread_segv_with_pkey0_disabled, waits on the global condition variable until siginfo.si_signo is non-zero, and then reports a ksft test result that passes exactly when siginfo.si_signo == SIGSEGV, siginfo.si_code == SEGV_MAPERR and siginfo.si_addr == NULL; it changes the SIGSEGV disposition, leaves the global siginfo filled with the fault's siginfo, and leaves the detached thread terminated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:205-236 and kept; pthread_create's result is not checked

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(migrate)
prose: Fixture teardown generated by FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(migrate) (rmap.c:195-220), void; it takes the fixture data self. Precondition: self->data was filled in by FIXTURE_SETUP(migrate) (which sets expected_pfn, semid, pipefd and backend but does not initialize data->region; the fixture data starts zeroed, so region is NULL, not MAP_FAILED, unless a test set it). Postcondition: it calls munmap(data->region, data->mapsize) if data->region is not MAP_FAILED (so also when it is still NULL, in which case munmap fails harmlessly) and sets it to MAP_FAILED; it unmaps data->expected_pfn if it is not MAP_FAILED and sets it to MAP_FAILED; it removes the semaphore set with semctl(IPC_RMID) and sets data->semid to -1; it closes the read end data->pipefd[0] (the write end is not closed here); and according to data->backend it calls shm_unlink(data->filename) for SHM, unlink(data->filename) for NORM_FILE and does nothing for ANON. Return values of these calls are ignored.
note: reviewer (round15) right: setup leaves data->region uninitialized/zero (rmap.c:159-193), so the old precondition 'region valid or MAP_FAILED' was inaccurate and region may be NULL at teardown. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: merge_and_migrate
prose: Precondition: data points to a struct global_data whose expected_pfn field points to a writable unsigned long; data->region may be any value (MAP_FAILED is handled). Postcondition (merge_and_migrate, rmap.c:389-408): it returns FAIL_ON_WORK at once if data->region is MAP_FAILED, and returns FAIL_ON_WORK if ksm_start() fails (negative result); neither case needs KSM to be available beforehand since both failures are handled. Otherwise it calls try_to_move_page(data->region) and keeps its result (0 on success or FAIL_ON_WORK), then opens /proc/self/pagemap; if that open fails it returns FAIL_ON_WORK (the try_to_move_page result is discarded), otherwise it stores the PFN of data->region read from pagemap in *data->expected_pfn and returns the try_to_move_page result. The pagemap descriptor is opened only after the page was moved and is never closed (leaked).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the function handles a MAP_FAILED region and a failing ksm_start itself (rmap.c:394-398), so the old precondition requiring a valid region and KSM was unnecessary; the pagemap descriptor leak and the ordering (move first, then pagemap) from the old prose were right and are kept.

name: uffd_wp_unpopulated_test
prose: Precondition: gopts->uffd is a valid userfaultfd and gopts->area_dst is a mapping of at least gopts->nr_pages * gopts->page_size bytes (it need not be registered; the function registers it). Postcondition (uffd_wp_unpopulated_test, uffd-unit-tests.c:338-382; returns void): it registers the whole area with uffd_register for write-protect mode (err() terminates the test on failure) and opens a pagemap descriptor (never closed). On the first page it then: write-protects it with wp_range and checks that the pagemap entry has the wp bit set; unprotects it and checks the bit is clear; write-protects it again, zaps it with MADV_DONTNEED (err() on failure) and checks the bit is clear; writes to the page (fault-in) and checks the bit is clear, then drops it with MADV_DONTNEED; write-protects it again, reads it (the read of the zero page, with no pagemap check) and drops it with MADV_DONTNEED. It ends with uffd_test_pass(). The range stays registered and the pagemap descriptor stays open.
note: reviewer (round15) right: no pagemap check follows the read-zero-page step (uffd-unit-tests.c:374-379); the wp bit is checked after protect, unprotect, zap and fault-in only. Round-0 reviewer's point (the function registers the area itself) was already right in the old prose.

name: uffd_wp_fork_pin_test_common
prose: Precondition: gopts->uffd is a valid userfaultfd and gopts->area_dst is a mapping of at least gopts->page_size bytes (the function registers the first page itself); with_event selects whether fork events are used in the child checks. Postcondition (uffd_wp_fork_pin_test_common, uffd-unit-tests.c:464-515; returns void): it registers the first page for write-protect mode (err() on failure), opens a pagemap descriptor, touches the page and write-protects it. It tries to pin the page (pin_pages): if that fails it marks the test skipped, closes the pagemap descriptor, calls uffd_unregister (its result is ignored on this path) and returns. Otherwise it runs pagemap_test_fork(gopts, with_event, false) (fork after pinning, the early-copy path); if that reports a wrong child wp bit it calls uffd_test_fail, unpins and goes to the out label; otherwise it unpins and runs pagemap_test_fork(gopts, with_event, true) (pin in the child); a failure there calls uffd_test_fail and goes to out, and success calls uffd_test_pass. At out it unregisters the page (err() terminates the test if that fails) and closes the pagemap descriptor.
note: reviewer (round15) right: on the skip path the uffd_unregister result is not checked (uffd-unit-tests.c:488), so 'on every path it unregisters the page, aborting via err() if that fails' was too broad; round-0 reviewer's point (it registers the area itself) was already right.

name: default_huge_page_size
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (default_huge_page_size, vm_util.c:294-313): if /proc/meminfo cannot be opened it returns 0 immediately (nothing has been allocated or opened at that point). Otherwise it reads the file line by line with getline until the first line that matches 'Hugepagesize: <number> kB', takes that number shifted left by 10 (kB to bytes) as the result and stops reading; if no line matches the result is 0. On every path that opened the file it frees the getline buffer and closes the stream before returning the result.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong in substance but right on precision: on fopen failure there is no buffer to free and no stream to close (line is NULL, f is NULL, vm_util.c:297-302), so the old prose is true on the paths that opened the file; the prose now states the early return explicitly.

name: get_free_hugepages
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (get_free_hugepages, vm_util.c:399-416): if /proc/meminfo cannot be opened it returns 0 immediately (nothing has been allocated or opened at that point). Otherwise it reads the file line by line with getline until the first line that matches 'HugePages_Free: <number>', stores that number as the result and stops reading; if no line matches the result is 0. On every path that opened the file it frees the getline buffer and closes the stream before returning the result.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong in substance but right on precision: nothing is allocated or opened when fopen fails (vm_util.c:402-407); the prose now states the early return explicitly.

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped)
prose: Fixture setup generated by FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped) (mount_setattr_test.c:994-1052; the packet slices split it at line 1024), void. Precondition: the process can unshare a mount namespace and mount filesystems (CAP_SYS_ADMIN); /tmp, /mnt and the tools mkfs.ext4 and mount exist. Postcondition: it unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / recursively private (ASSERT_EQ 0 each), lazily unmounts /mnt and /tmp (results ignored), then mounts a tmpfs (NOATIME, NODEV, size=100000, mode=700) on /tmp and creates /tmp/B with a root-owned regular file /tmp/B/b, mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B, creates /tmp/B/BB with a root-owned file /tmp/B/BB/b and mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B/BB. It mounts a tmpfs (size=256m, mode=700) on /mnt and creates /mnt/A with a tmpfs mounted on it, /mnt/A/AA with a recursive bind mount of /tmp on it, /mnt/B with a ramfs mounted on it (NOATIME, NODEV, NOSUID) and /mnt/B/BB (just a directory), mounts a read-only devpts (RELATIME, NOEXEC, RDONLY) on /tmp/B/BB (not on /mnt/B/BB), creates /mnt/C and /mnt/D, creates /mnt/C/ext4.img of 2 GiB, formats it with mkfs.ext4 and loop-mounts it as ext4 on /mnt/D through system() calls (each asserted to return 0), and closes the image descriptor. Every step except the two umount2 calls is an ASSERT, so a failure aborts the test instead of returning.
note: reviewer (round15) right on the related claim: umount2 failures are ignored (mount_setattr_test.c:1002-1003), so 'any failing step aborts' is false for those two calls; this prose covers the whole fixture setup (the second half of the same function is in the next slice). Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped)
prose: Fixture setup generated by FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped) (mount_setattr_test.c:994-1052; the packet slices split it at line 1024), void. Precondition: the process can unshare a mount namespace and mount filesystems (CAP_SYS_ADMIN); /tmp, /mnt and the tools mkfs.ext4 and mount exist. Postcondition: it unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / recursively private (ASSERT_EQ 0 each), lazily unmounts /mnt and /tmp (results ignored), then mounts a tmpfs (NOATIME, NODEV, size=100000, mode=700) on /tmp and creates /tmp/B with a root-owned regular file /tmp/B/b, mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B, creates /tmp/B/BB with a root-owned file /tmp/B/BB/b and mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B/BB. It mounts a tmpfs (size=256m, mode=700) on /mnt and creates /mnt/A with a tmpfs mounted on it, /mnt/A/AA with a recursive bind mount of /tmp on it, /mnt/B with a ramfs mounted on it (NOATIME, NODEV, NOSUID) and /mnt/B/BB (just a directory), mounts a read-only devpts (RELATIME, NOEXEC, RDONLY) on /tmp/B/BB (not on /mnt/B/BB), creates /mnt/C and /mnt/D, creates /mnt/C/ext4.img of 2 GiB, formats it with mkfs.ext4 and loop-mounts it as ext4 on /mnt/D through system() calls (each asserted to return 0), and closes the image descriptor. Every step except the two umount2 calls is an ASSERT, so a failure aborts the test instead of returning.
note: reviewer (round15) right: devpts is mounted at /tmp/B/BB (mount_setattr_test.c:1041), not /mnt/B/BB, and /tmp/B/BB is first a tmpfs and then a devpts is mounted over it; /mnt/B/BB is only a directory. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: TEST_F(mount_setattr, mount_detached_mount_on_detached_mount_and_attach)

Precondition: the mount_setattr fixture setup has built its mount layout (a testing tmpfs on /mnt, /mnt/A with its tree, /mnt/B a ramfs, /tmp/B a tmpfs) and /tmp/target1 exists. Postcondition: it opens a detached (non-recursive) clone of /mnt (fd_tree_base) and asserts through statx that its subdirectory A is not a mount root; it opens a second detached clone from fd_tree_base itself (fd_tree_subdir, with AT_EMPTY_PATH) and makes the same check. It moves fd_tree_subdir onto fd_tree_base with move_mount (asserted to succeed), asserts that fd_tree_subdir is now a mount root with a unique mount id and records that id, and asserts that a second identical move_mount fails. It then attaches fd_tree_base to /tmp/target1 (asserted to succeed) and asserts that /tmp/target1 is a mount root whose unique mount id equals the recorded id. Finally it closes both tree fds (EXPECT_EQ 0, recorded failures only). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.

name: TEST_F(mount_setattr, basic_recursive)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mount_setattr, basic_recursive) (mount_setattr_test.c:565-657); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the mount_setattr fixture built its layout (/mnt/A, /mnt/A/AA, /mnt/A/AA/B, /mnt/A/AA/B/BB); if the mount_setattr syscall is not supported the test skips and returns. Postcondition: it reads the flags of /mnt/A, then calls sys_mount_setattr on /mnt/A with AT_RECURSIVE setting RDONLY, NOEXEC and RELATIME and clearing the atime bits (ASSERT_EQ 0), and asserts that all four mounts have the expected flags. It then calls it again recursively with only MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY cleared and propagation MS_SHARED (ASSERT_EQ 0) and asserts that all four mounts have the expected flags without RDONLY and are shared. It opens /mnt/A/AA/B/b for writing (O_CREAT | O_EXCL), calls the recursive setattr once more with attr_set = MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY and asserts that it fails (return < 0, because a writer is open) and that the flags and shared state of all four mounts are unchanged, then closes the file (EXPECT_EQ 0). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the RDONLY-clearing/MS_SHARED call succeeds before the file is opened, and the call made while the file is open must fail (mount_setattr_test.c:600-634); the old prose had the order reversed.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc is 1 or 2 (any other count is treated like the default case, because only argc == 2 selects a queue name); argv[1], if given, is the message-queue name. Postcondition (main, mq_open_tests.c:239-502; slice cut the head; it never returns): it chooses the queue path: the default path, or argv[1] (with a leading '/' added when missing; a malloc failure calls exit(1) and the result of strdup is not checked). If the user is not root it calls ksft_exit_skip, which exits. It opens the msg_max and msgsize_max /proc/sys files (and the default-setting files when present); if msg_max or msgsize_max cannot be opened it calls shutdown(2, ...). It saves the current sysctl values and RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE (the helpers it uses call shutdown with a nonzero status on read, write or rlimit errors), prints the initial and the adjusted system state, and runs test series 1 (mq_open without an attr struct, with different cases depending on whether default settings are supported) and test series 2 (mq_open with attr structs that exceed limits, first with euid 0 and then, after seteuid(99), with euid 99; a failing seteuid(99) calls exit(1) directly), printing PASS or FAIL lines; the test_queue helpers call shutdown(1, ...) if an mq call fails unexpectedly. It ends with shutdown(0, "", 0), which restores euid 0, closes and unlinks the queue, restores the saved sysctl and rlimit values and calls exit(0); a nonzero shutdown status instead reports the error with error(status, ...) and exits with that status.
note: slice cut the head. Reviewer (round15) right: the early fopen failures call shutdown(2, ...) and other helper failures call shutdown(1/4-7, ...) (mq_open_tests.c:123-213, 279-281), so main does not always end in shutdown(0); the old prose also implied exit(1) for 'seteuid or malloc' only.

name: TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation) (file_handle_test.c:1226-1373; the packet name nsfs_open_by_handle_from_user_ns does not exist and the slice starts mid-test); it takes _metadata and returns void. Precondition: the kernel provides time namespaces and nsfs file handles, otherwise the test skips and returns (after freeing the handle and closing its descriptors). Postcondition: it allocates a file handle (ASSERT_NE NULL), creates a pipe, opens /proc/self/ns/time and gets its handle with name_to_handle_at (EOPNOTSUPP skips; any other failure fails ASSERT_EQ(ret, 0)), then forks. The child unshares a user namespace, maps the current uid and gid to 0 (after writing 'deny' to setgroups), unshares a time namespace, forks a grandchild and waits for it, then exits 0; if the user-namespace unshare fails it writes 'U' to the pipe, if opening or writing the maps fails it writes 'M' (the write calls themselves are unchecked), if the time-namespace unshare or the inner fork fails it writes 'N', and exits 0 in each of those cases. The grandchild calls open_by_handle_at on the parent's time-namespace handle and writes 'S' if that unexpectedly succeeds, 'P' if it fails with ESTALE and 'F' for any other error, then exits 0. The parent closes the write end, reads one byte (ASSERT_EQ 1), reaps the child and asserts that it exited normally with status 0, skips on 'U', 'M' or 'N', and otherwise asserts that the byte is 'P'. It then closes the pipe and frees the handle.
note: slice cut the head; real test is TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation); the old prose was essentially right (it also correctly listed the 'U'/'M'/'N' skips) and is expanded with the setup and parent-side checks.

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(unix_sock)
prose: Fixture teardown generated by FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(unix_sock) (unix_connreset.c:89-98), void; it takes the fixture data self and the variant. Precondition: FIXTURE_SETUP(unix_sock) has run, but the test may already have closed some of the descriptors, and self->child is set only if the test accepted a connection (the fixture data starts zeroed, so it is 0 otherwise). Postcondition: for the SOCK_STREAM and SOCK_SEQPACKET variants it calls close(self->child) (which may close descriptor 0 if child was never set, or fail on a descriptor the test already closed); for all variants it then calls close(self->client) and close(self->server) (either may already be closed by the test, in which case the call just fails) and unlinks the socket path /tmp/af_unix_connreset.sock. The return values are ignored.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the old precondition 'fixture fds are open' is false after tests such as eof, which close child or server themselves and leave self->child unset (0) otherwise (unix_connreset.c:101-114). Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).
